patch.value:
Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1469

**Type:** prevention/design proposal, with existing delivered foundations retained.

### Problem and boundary

The existing terminal-defect gate already requires escape classification and structured gate evidence for post-epoch terminal Issues and bug/defect/security-tagged items, independently of recurrence edges. Its [validator](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/0e94c3c773a73a408b298208843d10eb0e553688/src/sdk/governance/defect-recurrence.ts#L948-L1105) validates an owner, disposition and nonempty gate/test/negative-control fields. That is useful evidence governance, but those strings do not themselves establish which test executed, what population it covered, whether it detected the original failure or which artifact it certified.

The recorded recurrence graph has a separate, intentionally narrower [local recurs_from population](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/0e94c3c773a73a408b298208843d10eb0e553688/src/sdk/governance/defect-recurrence-graph.ts#L44-L63). Do not replace that denominator with every report, manufacture recurrence edges or add another classification gate.

A concrete population hole is the [core-only flag invocation gate](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/0e94c3c773a73a408b298208843d10eb0e553688/scripts/release/flag-invocation-parity.mjs#L38-L46). Its scope is explicitly value arity: [repeatability is copied from declarations and owned by a separate grammar gate](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/0e94c3c773a73a408b298208843d10eb0e553688/scripts/release/flag-invocation-parity.mjs#L99-L130). It must not be reported as independent proof of every flag semantic. #1466 and #1467 demonstrate distinct behavioral and discovery gaps without invalidating the useful existing core check.

This is a narrow follow-on to [pm-rtn5h6](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/tasks/pm-rtn5h6.toon), [pm-0pzgit](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/tasks/pm-0pzgit.toon) and [pm-7c27ep](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/issues/pm-7c27ep.toon), not a reopening of their delivered scope. Reuse existing runner, gate registry, linked tests, evidence storage and SDK verdict primitives. Existing artifact-ledger reconciliation already checks complete exact identity inventories; reuse that primitive where appropriate rather than adding a second release inventory. This proposal joins incident/test/fixture proof to actual execution, not a claim that existing CI tests never execute. Coordinate first-party package adoption through the existing open [pm-feecbs](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/features/pm-feecbs.toon) ecosystem-conformance owner. Start with the core host plus deterministic extension fixtures; broader package adoption remains there, with explicit coverage limits until completed.

### Implementation plan

1. Add a versioned, additive **proof reference/receipt** to existing gate evidence. Resolve stable test/fixture IDs against the existing runner; never execute arbitrary command strings read from tracker items. Human prose can explain evidence but cannot manufacture a pass.
2. A receipt identifies its claim/owner, criterion or invariant, test and fixture content digests, runner/policy version, declared and executed case identities, source revision, lock/runtime/OS identity, verdict, failure category and durable sanitized evidence location.
3. For artifact claims, also bind the package/version, package integrity or tarball digest, installation mode and actual resolved entrypoint. Distinguish source, packed-candidate and published-installed evidence. Derive these from the runner/build inputs rather than author-supplied labels.
4. Record the original failing revision/artifact and the passing candidate using the **same independent fixture and asserted failure signature**. Assert the bad behavior, not merely any nonzero exit. Version-specific launch adapters are allowed only with recorded identities and the unchanged semantic oracle; they must not erase the behavior being tested. When the historical artifact is unavailable, report missing evidence; when only a targeted mutant or source reconstruction is available, label that weaker scope rather than claiming a historical reproduction.
5. Validate receipt references at closure and at the applicable CI/release gate. Cheap validation is allowed to reuse content-addressed passing evidence only when its artifact, fixtures, runner, dependencies and policy inputs are unchanged. A linked URL, stale head, empty case set or nonempty text is not equivalent to an execution.
6. Reconcile independent source populations for core commands, supported first-party extension commands and package SDK exports. Introspect the executable registration/loaded extension surface, machine contracts and actual package manifest/export resolution separately, then fail on missing/extra identities or unexplained exclusions. Enumerate semantic fixture partitions from the public extension schema; this cannot claim exhaustive coverage of arbitrary third-party extensions.
7. Extend existing parity/acceptance fixtures at the demonstrated gaps first: #1466 boolean alias values, #1467 optional arity, and #1464 success/follow-up transport. Preserve first affected old/new storage artifact pairs from #1458/#1468 through the existing compatibility policy rather than replacing it with a moving latest-two window.
8. Keep complete-set checks separate from pagination/projection of reports. Every selected test has an explicit terminal verdict. Required skipped, missing, stale, inconclusive, unexecuted, unsupported-platform or zero-case results block the stage that requires them.

### Fixture-validity contract

- External boundary expectations continue to require captured provider output wherever the existing boundary policy requires it, with version/provenance and redaction metadata in the **existing** inventory. An independent format specification/reference oracle can supplement that sample, not replace a required capture. A provenance string alone does not prove independence; review the capture path and retain executable fault controls.
- Internal semantic fixtures may be synthetic, but expected results must not call the production normalizer/formatter under test. A shared declaration can be the production authority; a separately reviewed literal observation or small reference model must own the oracle.
- Keep fixture schema validation, execution and semantic verdict distinct. A malformed fixture, exception before the target assertion, timeout or missing provider is a harness/evidence failure, not proof the product mutant was detected.
- Redaction must preserve the exact feature that caused the mismatch, such as underscores, nested field structure, false versus absent, literal quoting or sparse array holes. JSON serialization cannot stand in for native JS values that JSON cannot represent.
- Use synthetic non-sensitive workspaces by default. Retain necessary legal/licensing information with captures. No user workspace, session transcript, private path, secret, telemetry payload or credentials in committed fixtures.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A post-epoch terminal defect outside the recurrence graph still fails the existing evidence policy when proof is required and missing; no artificial recurs_from edge is needed.
- [ ] Resolver negative controls reject unknown test IDs, missing fixture/receipt files, wrong fixture digest, wrong revision/artifact, stale policy, forged case counts, zero selected cases and skipped required assertions.
- [ ] A valid envelope containing an infrastructure failure cannot count as the expected pre-fix failure or a candidate pass.
- [ ] At least one baseline/candidate fixture pair demonstrates the original semantic failure before and passing behavior after, with unchanged oracle and sanitized raw receipts. If the assigned fix is still open, its receipt remains failing rather than altering the oracle to make it green.
- [ ] Core, first-party extension and SDK population discovery are independently complete within their declared scope. Deliberately omit/add an extension command, a core command contract and a manifest SDK export; each produces a named missing/extra-case failure. Counts and exclusions are exposed, not only an aggregate percentage.
- [ ] Extension observations cover bare/equals/spaced/negated boolean forms, true/false and 1/0, required/optional values, aliases, nested/flattened commands, repeated values and meaningful positional arguments through help, contracts, actual dispatch and relevant SDK consumers. Select orthogonal cases and known risky interactions; do not require the entire Cartesian product per PR.
- [ ] Required compatibility rows retain exact nested values, original history prefixes and unchanged-byte refusal across read, ordinary write, restore and native merge. Keep the existing historical versions and moving prior-release window.
- [ ] Each gate states precisely what it proves: selection activation, fixture validity, signature parity, behavior, mutation detection, compatibility or installed consumer acceptance. Selection-only negative controls cannot be labeled product-defect controls.
- [ ] Exact final-head checks, packed acceptance and published-installed acceptance remain separately visible. Source/packed success cannot satisfy a published-fix claim.
- [ ] Existing exact coverage, mutation floors, timeouts, performance budgets, mandatory workflow contexts, source membership and exclusions are not weakened.

### Rollout and proportionality

Introduce the receipt reader and negative controls first, keeping legacy evidence readable and explicitly marked “recorded, execution binding not migrated.” Start enforcement prospectively on newly fixed defects and touched high-risk evidence; backfill the recent demonstrated families and permanent historic counterexamples. Do not reclose thousands of items or invent missing historical runs.

Use the existing recurrence/change-risk selectors and dependency/export relationships for incremental **additional** tests. Changes to a shared normalizer, output engine, serialization/storage layer, exported schema, gate runner or selection policy trigger the relevant broad suite. Unknown selection mapping fails closed or runs that suite; it never silently selects none. Retain existing mandatory full gates. Deterministic small keepers run on affected PRs; expanded mutation and historical matrices run in their appropriate mandatory CI/release stages. A native-OS row can run on its native worker; Linux “skipped” is not that worker's passing evidence.

Prefer reviewed cache bundles for historical public artifacts. Separate controlled acquisition from offline execution, verify integrity, disable install scripts where possible, isolate HOME/PM/Git configuration, disable telemetry and deny test network access. Required artifacts unavailable offline make that stage unavailable/blocked, not passed. No new credentials, model calls, server, user data or network bypass is required.

Publication is a separate authorized process. After approved publication, resolve the exact public version/integrity and rerun installed acceptance; a publication failure or visibility delay remains pending. Do not republish a different artifact under an immutable version or rewrite historical receipts.

### Suggested implementation locations

- Existing SDK evidence: src/sdk/governance/defect-recurrence.ts and assurance public schemas
- Existing runner/registry integration: scripts/release/defect-evidence-gate.mjs, gate-registry, run-gates and linked-test receipts
- Existing fixture integrity: src/sdk/governance/boundary-fixtures.ts and config/boundary-fixtures.json
- Existing surface checks: flag-invocation-parity, command-grammar, package-sdk-contract-parity and public SDK surface checks
- Existing compatibility: scripts/release/workspace-compatibility.mjs, workspace-linked-tests.mjs and workspace-compatibility-policy.json

Exact new names and receipt storage should follow the implementation inventory; these are integration points, not a mandate for a parallel subsystem.
GH-1469: Bind defect evidence to executed exact-artifact regression receipts
Prospective execution binding for existing defect evidence, preserving distinct source, packed and published claims and existing immutable evidence contracts.

Resolve stable fixture/test identities using the existing runner, never arbitrary tracker commands; Bind declared/executed cases and verdicts to source/artifact/runner/policy identities; Reject missing, stale, skipped, zero-case and forged proof; Preserve historical evidence without inventing execution; Reuse existing assurance, recurrence, fixture and artifact reconciliation primitives
